AlternateTargets: the manner of a house or lineage
Senses.Explanation: Literally 'the wind/manner of a house.' In the records it names the distinctive teaching-style and household-manner of a particular master or lineage — how THIS house does things. Its commonest form is the stock interview question 'What is the master's family style?' (如何是和尚家風), which the master answers with a concrete, homely image of his own place and way: 'white clouds come and close the door' (Tianzhu), 'harvest in autumn, store away in winter,' or 'my old ears are deaf — ask louder' (adding, 'you ask MY house-style, but I already know YOURS'). The word is used equally of a single teacher (和尚家風) and of a whole lineage or the tradition at large — (臨濟家風) (the Linji house's way), (佛祖家風) / (古佛家風) (the way of the buddhas and ancestors), (野老家風) (the plain 'old rustic's' style). The register is domestic and self-characterizing, often plain ('eating gruel, eating rice — also to be done carefully'): the recognizable style, temper and household-manner a teacher hands down, by which one house is told from another. Zen-scoped grep counts: (家風) 3743 hits across 335 of the 462 allowlist texts; the interview question (如何是)…(家風) accounts for 1173 hits in 141 texts, of which the exact (如何是和尚家風) makes 819 in 113. Scale collocations: (古佛家風) 209/113, (臨濟家風) 64/46, (佛祖家風) 54/42, (野老家風) 20/15, (衲僧家風) 5/4. The records also use it as a verdict of succession: (吾宗門下曹山可謂妙得其家風者) (within our school, Caoshan may be said to have marvelously gotten his family-wind; J40nB494), with the same formula (可謂妙得其家風者) said of another heir at J34nB299.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense: the term is a shared, house-neutral word applied to every master and lineage, not bent by any single master. Extremely broad attestation (3743 occurrences in 335 allowlist files, tag-stripped re-concordance 2026-07-11; an earlier count of ~613 was low), so multi-source is beyond doubt. No master-specific sense warranted.
